critical_findings: Severe global lighting/color drift between baseline and candidate; candidate becomes dramatically darker and red-tinted.
Helmet shell change is not cleanly readable as a controlled dark green material edit because the altered lighting makes it appear nearly black/green-black.
Overall scene continuity is degraded by the unintended appearance change across walls, sofa, floor, and table.

scores.evidence: Sofa, coffee table, floor lamp, and helmet are all present; the coffee table is visibly closer to the sofa in the candidate views, and the helmet shell is no longer red-looking in the revised shots.
The candidate introduces a major camera/scene presentation drift: the baseline bright neutral lighting becomes a dark red/orange-tinted look, substantially changing the composition's readability.

Lighting and material appearance shift heavily between baseline and candidate; the sofa, floor, walls, and table all take on a deep reddish cast, obscuring the intended selective helmet-only material change.

The helmet reads very dark, but under the altered lighting it is difficult to verify a clean dark-green shell finish; the visible result looks closer to black/green-black than a clearly controlled material edit.

The revision is not visually continuous with the baseline due to strong global lighting/color drift, making the intended isolated edit difficult to trust even though the table position change is apparent.
